ai.title: Gate think tag instructions to default and max modes
ai.summary: `base2.ts` gates the `<think>` tag instruction to `isDefault || isMax` modes only, removing it from lite and fast paths. The quick-problem guidance now directs the agent to briefly explain reasoning to the user instead of relying on hidden tags. `isOpus` flag switches from hardcoded `true` to `!isLite`, aligning model selection with mode. Affects internal agent prompt construction in `.agents/base2/base2.ts`.

eli5.text: On January 4, 2026, an internal tweak to the agent's decision logic made hidden reasoning tags only available in the standard and most capable operating modes, quietly removing them from the lightweight and fast modes. If you watched the assistant work in the lightweight mode, you'd now see it briefly explain its next steps out loud instead of tucking reasoning into hidden scratch space; in the default and most capable modes, that behind-the-scenes note-taking behavior stays available for complex planning. The change also nudges model selection so that anything not labeled lightweight leans on the more capable default model, nudging overall performance toward that tier. ai.title: Enable askuser step in base2 agent prompt
ai.summary: The `ask_user` tool is now explicitly included in the `base2` agent's workflow steps when `noAskUser` is false. Previously, this instruction was only added for `isMax` configurations and framed as an optional "if needed" step. The change ensures the agent proactively seeks clarifications after gathering context, unless explicitly disabled. This affects the internal prompt generation logic in `.agents/base2/base2.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask the coding assistant a question, it first reads through relevant files to understand the codebase, and it now automatically checks in with you for important clarifications before proceeding to write code. Previously, it only paused to ask follow-up questions when working at its highest power setting, and even then only "if needed." Now, by default, the assistant actively asks you targeted questions after gathering context, unless that behavior is explicitly turned off. If you watched a session, you would notice the assistant inserting a clarification step right after it finishes reading files and before it starts implementing changes.

ai.title: Anthropic token count API replaces local estimation in context pruner
ai.summary: Added /api/v1/token-count endpoint proxying Anthropic API and callTokenCountAPI client. Context pruner now uses agentState.contextTokenCount updated every step, replacing countMessagesTokens estimation. Scope includes agent-runtime, common types, web API, and analytics events. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY server env.

eli5.text: The assistant now gets an exact count of how full your conversation is from Anthropic's servers each step, instead of guessing. This more accurate count powers the context pruner, so it knows precisely when your conversation is about to hit the limit and when it is safe to skip trimming. Right now this runs automatically as each agent step executes, with no extra action needed from you.

ai.title: Context pruner replaces heuristic trimming with LLM summarization
ai.summary: The `context-pruner` agent now uses a single-pass LLM summarization strategy instead of multi-pass heuristic trimming. Old logic removed orphaned tool calls, truncated large results, and aggressively pruned non-important messages; new logic condenses the entire conversation history into a single user-role summary message when context exceeds `maxContextLength`. Target summary size is 15% of max context (`TARGET_SUMMARY_FACTOR = 0.15`). Long individual messages are truncated to 80% prefix / 20% suffix (`USER_MESSAGE_LIMIT = 20000`, `ASSISTANT_MESSAGE_LIMIT = 5000`) before summarization.

eli5.text: When your conversation with the assistant gets very long (near the 200,000-word limit), the system now replaces all that old back-and-forth with a single, concise summary message instead of simply cutting out pieces it thinks matter less. This means you keep more of the story without losing important details, because the summary captures the whole conversation in roughly one-sixth the space (15% of the limit). Long individual messages, whether from you or the assistant, are trimmed to keep the most important beginning and end before that summary is created, and this new behavior is live today in the agent’s context-pruning step.

ai.title: Strip think tags in context pruner
ai.summary: Context pruner now strips `<think>` tags and contents before summarizing text parts in `.agents/context-pruner.ts`. Prevents internal reasoning traces from polluting pruned context summaries. Affects internal agent context management only.

eli5.text: Your internal assistant tools occasionally get confused when they accidentally include their own behind-the-scenes reasoning in the summarized notes they pass around. The system now quietly removes those thinking sections before packaging up the notes, so the summary stays focused on what actually happened instead of getting muddled with the assistant's private deliberation. Only internal tooling is affected, and this is already active.

ai.title: Fix CLI sluggishness by removing unnecessary re-renders
ai.summary: Stabilized `streamingAgents` reference in `cli/src/chat.tsx` using `useMemo` on a sorted key, preventing re-renders when Set content is unchanged. Memoized `onOpenFeedback` callback in `cli/src/components/message-with-agents.tsx` via `useCallback` to avoid prop identity changes. Scope limited to CLI React components. These changes address performance issues caused by unstable references triggering excessive UI updates.

eli5.text: When you chat with the assistant in the terminal, the screen used to feel sluggish because parts of it were redrawing themselves even when nothing changed. The team tuned the assistant list and feedback button so they only update when their actual content changes, cutting down on those wasteful redraws. You would notice the terminal responding more smoothly as you type and navigate conversations, with less flickering or pausing when new agent activity appears. This fix is live today for anyone using the terminal-based assistant interface.

ai.title: Add CODEBUFFPERFTEST env flag for CLI re-render diagnostics
ai.summary: New `CODEBUFF_PERF_TEST` environment variable gates `useWhyDidYouUpdateById` logging in `AgentBranchItem` and `MessageBlock`. Previously hardcoded `false`, these components now check `getCliEnv().CODEBUFF_PERF_TEST === 'true'` to enable debug-level render tracking. The flag is added to `CliEnv` types and `getCliEnv` utility in `cli/src/types/env.ts` and `cli/src/utils/env.ts`. This allows developers to diagnose unnecessary re-renders in the CLI TUI without code changes.

eli5.text: If you run the CLI with a new hidden switch turned on, it will start printing debug notes about which parts of the screen are drawing themselves repeatedly and unnecessarily; this only happens when that switch is active, so most people will see nothing different today. The change adds a new environment variable called CODEBUFF_PERF_TEST; when set to 'true', the CLI logs detailed re-render diagnostics for the message display and conversation branch components. Developers working on the CLI can use this flag to identify and fix sluggishness caused by redundant interface updates without modifying any code.

ai.title: Exclude integration tests from default bun test run
ai.summary: bunfig.toml now adds `**/*.integration.test.*` to the default test exclude list. This prevents long-running integration tests from executing during standard `bun test` invocations, reducing noise and potential timeouts. Scope is limited to the root `bunfig.toml` configuration.

eli5.text: When you run the standard test command to check that the codebase still works, it now skips the long-running integration tests that test how different parts connect together. Previously, those heavier tests were included by default, which could slow things down or cause timeouts during routine checks. You would notice fewer tests running and faster feedback when triggering the normal test suite, while the integration tests are still available to run separately when needed.

ai.title: Remove committed eval error output files
ai.summary: Deleted 24 `*-agent-output-error.json` files from `evals/` that were accidentally committed. These files contained agent run failure traces and error messages from eval executions. This cleanup prevents stale error artifacts from polluting the repository and ensures eval outputs are not tracked in version control.

eli5.text: The development team deleted 24 temporary error log files that were accidentally saved in the project's main storage area. These files contained records of automated test failures ('Failed to start agent run') and were never meant to be permanently kept. If you browsed the project folder, you would no longer see these outdated error reports cluttering the test results directory. This is routine cleanup that keeps the project organized so only intentional, current files are tracked.

ai.title: Delete dead evals code
ai.summary: Removed unused agent execution and test setup logic from `evals/scaffolding.ts` and deleted `evals/test-setup.ts`. `TEST_REPOS_DIR` now defined inline in `evals/buffbench/setup-test-repo.ts`. Imports for `runAgentStep`, `assembleLocalAgentTemplates`, and `ToolHelpers` stripped from `scaffolding.ts`.

eli5.text: The team cleaned out some old, unused testing tools that were left over from earlier experiments - roughly 470 lines of code were removed while only 2 were added. This is behind-the-scenes maintenance that makes the system a bit leaner and easier to maintain going forward, but you wouldn't notice any difference in how the product works today.

ai.title: CLI test-utils isTmuxAvailable verifies tmux usability
ai.summary: The `isTmuxAvailable` helper in `cli/src/__tests__/test-utils.ts` now verifies tmux usability by creating and killing a temporary session, rather than just checking for the binary. This change ensures the function returns false in environments like GitHub Actions where the tmux server socket directory is inaccessible, preventing false positives. The update is scoped to CLI test utilities and includes a 5-second timeout for the session check.

eli5.text: The assistant now double-checks that its terminal-multiplexing tool is not just installed but actually usable before relying on it during testing. Previously, it only confirmed the tool existed, which gave false "yes" answers in automated environments where the tool's background service can't start. If you watched the startup sequence, you'd see it briefly spin up and tear down a throwaway test session, timing out after five seconds if the service never kicks in. The developers noted this only affects internal test tooling, so day-to-day usage stays the same.

ai.title: Prune context on 5-minute cache expiry
ai.summary: Context pruning now triggers on prompt cache expiry, not just token limits. The `context-pruner` detects gaps >5 minutes between the last assistant message and the current `USER_PROMPT`, forcing a fresh summary to avoid cache miss costs. Added `sentAt` timestamps to `AuxiliaryMessageData` in `common` and `agent-runtime` to track message age. The `sentAt` field is stripped before sending to the LLM.

eli5.text: When you come back to a conversation after the assistant has been quietly waiting for five minutes or more, it now clears out the old back-and-forth and writes you a fresh short summary of what was happening, so you don't waste money or wait time on a slow cache reload. The assistant quietly stamps each message with a clock time as it goes and checks that time the moment you ask something; if the gap is more than five minutes, it triggers the summary instead of just trimming words. This runs live today whenever a conversation goes idle for that five-minute stretch.

ai.title: Skip tmux integration tests on CI
ai.summary: isTmuxAvailable returns false when process.env.CI is true or 1. Prevents rerender-perf.integration.test.ts from running in GitHub Actions. Removes .catch(() => {}) from tmux set-environment calls. Reorders console.log statements in analysis output.

eli5.text: When the tool runs its performance tests in the cloud (GitHub Actions), it now automatically skips the special terminal testing that was causing problems. This means you'll see fewer failed test runs and less noise in the build logs, since the tests that needed a real interactive terminal are simply skipped in the automated environment. If you look at the build output, you won't see the tmux integration test errors anymore. The change is live today and affects anyone reviewing the automated test results.

ai.title: Update messages.test.ts assertions for sentAt
ai.summary: Added `sentAt: expect.any(Number)` to multiple test cases in `common/src/util/__tests__/messages.test.ts`. Removed `satisfies AssistantModelMessage` type assertion from one test case. This aligns tests with the `sentAt` field in model messages.

eli5.text: The assistant now attaches a timestamp to each message when it converts internal messages into the format the model reads, so every message in the log carries a record of when it was generated. When reviewing these logs, you will see a new numeric field (a number) next to user, assistant, and system messages that was missing before. This is a behind-the-scenes update to the automated checks that verify how those messages are built, so the visible behavior for you as a user is unchanged. It is already live as part of the current code.

ai.summary: Token counting endpoint trims assistant text and JSON parts before sending to Anthropic. Error logs now include messages, system prompt, and model on API failure. Change isolated to `web/src/app/api/v1/token-count/_post.ts`.

eli5.text: When the system counts how many tokens a message uses, it now trims extra spaces from your text and JSON data before sending it, which should result in slightly more accurate counts. If the token-counting service has a problem, the error logs now include the full message content, system instructions, and model name to make troubleshooting easier. This affects the internal system that tracks token usage and is now live.
